title: Imperative Handle Patterns
description: Learn how to use useImperativeHandle and forwardRef to expose imperative methods from child components to parents.

data.text: React's declarative model encourages parents to pass props down and children to render UI up. But some interactions—focusing an input, triggering an animation, or scrolling to an element—are inherently imperative. **useImperativeHandle** lets a child selectively expose methods to a parent ref without breaking encapsulation.

A DOM ref gives a parent direct access to a child's DOM node. That is powerful but brittle: the parent becomes coupled to the child's internal markup. If the child changes its structure, every parent that reached into it breaks. `useImperativeHandle` lets the child define a stable, intentional API surface.

data.title: Encapsulation Trade-off
data.text: Imperative handles are a deliberate escape hatch from declarative programming. Use them sparingly and document the exposed API clearly.

data.title: Focusable Input with useImperativeHandle
data.content: A child component exposes a focus method to the parent.

data.text: `forwardRef` takes two generic parameters: the handle type and the props type. TypeScript will enforce that parents only call methods defined on the handle, preventing accidental access to internal refs or private state.

data.title: Type-Safe Imperative Handle
data.content: Defining a strict handle interface for compile-time safety.

rows: Parent controls input focus without DOM traversal
Parent opens/closes overlay without lifting state

data.title: Dependency Array
data.text: The third argument to useImperativeHandle is a dependency array. If your handle closes over changing values, include them so the handle stays in sync.

data.title: Create a Scrollable Container
data.description: Build a component that exposes a scrollTo method via useImperativeHandle.
steps: Create a forwardRef component with a scrollable div.
Use useImperativeHandle to expose scrollTo(top, behavior).
Wire the internal ref to the div and call scrollIntoView or scrollTo.
Consume it from a parent with a button that scrolls to a specific item.
data.expectedOutcome: A reusable scrollable container with a clean imperative API.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: useImperativeHandle lets children expose a curated API to parent refs.
forwardRef bridges React's ref system with TypeScript generics.
Always provide a dependency array to avoid stale closures.
Prefer declarative data flow; use imperative handles only for truly imperative interactions.
data.takeaway: Imperative handles give you escape valves when declarative props are not enough.
